kept.q: Neither of the two prefects ___ absent yesterday.
kept.explanation: "Neither" is a singular pronoun, so it must be followed by a singular verb. The correct verb here is "was".
kept.pidgin: "Neither" na singular word, so e dey take singular verb. Na "was" dey correct here.

kept.q: Each of the students in Mrs. Okafor's class ___ a copy of the novel.
kept.explanation: "Each" is singular, so the verb that follows it must also be singular. "Has" agrees correctly with "each".
kept.pidgin: "Each" na singular pronoun, so di verb wey follow am must be singular too. "Has" dey match am well well.

kept.q: The jury ___ unanimous in its decision after deliberating for three hours.
kept.explanation: "Jury" is a collective noun, and in this sentence it is acting as one single unit (they agreed together). So it takes the singular verb "is".
kept.pidgin: "Jury" na collective noun, and for dis sentence dem act as one body (dem agree together). So "is" dey correct as singular verb.

kept.q: Many a trader at Oyingbo market ___ lost goods during the flood.
kept.explanation: The phrase "many a" is always followed by a singular noun and a singular verb, even though the meaning is plural in sense. So "has" is correct.
kept.pidgin: "Many a" dey always follow wit singular noun and singular verb, even though e dey mean plenty. So na "has" correct.

kept.q: Not only the headmaster but also the teachers ___ expected to attend the meeting.
kept.explanation: When two subjects are joined by "not only...but also", the verb agrees with the subject closer to it. Since "teachers" (plural) is nearer, "are" is correct.
kept.pidgin: When "not only...but also" join two subjects, di verb go agree wit di one wey near am. Since "teachers" (plural) near pass, "are" correct.

kept.q: The number of students who passed the WASSCE English paper ___ increased steadily over the past five years.
kept.explanation: "The number of" is treated as a singular subject because it refers to one total figure. Therefore the singular verb "has" is correct.
kept.pidgin: "The number of" na singular subject because e dey talk about one total figure. So na singular verb "has" dey correct.

kept.q: A number of farmers in the community ___ affected by the recent drought.
kept.explanation: Unlike "the number of", the phrase "a number of" means "several" and is treated as plural. So the plural verb "were" is correct.
kept.pidgin: Unlike "the number of", "a number of" mean "plenty" and e dey take plural verb. So "were" dey correct here.
